# Numbers

במדבר

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers)

מסעות בני ישראל במדבר, מפקדי אוכלוסין, מרידות, חטא המרגלים, מלחמות ושלל חוקים.

Wanderings of the Israelites in the desert, census, rebellion, spies and war, interspersed with laws.

Sections: Chapter-Verse

Location: Tanakh/Torah

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Miqra according to the Masorah (Segments: 1288, License: CC-BY-SA)

Versions (En):
  - Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009 (Segments: 1288, License: CC-BY)
  - The Koren Jerusalem Bible (Segments: 1288, License: CC-BY-NC)
  - The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein (Segments: 1288, License: CC-BY)


## Chapter 1

###### Numbers 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/1:1)


וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר יְהֹוָ֧ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֛ה בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר סִינַ֖י בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד בְּאֶחָד֩ לַחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֜י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשֵּׁנִ֗ית לְצֵאתָ֛ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לֵאמֹֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
And Adonoy spoke to Moshe in the Sinai desert, in the Tent of Meeting, on the first [day] of the second month, in the second year of their exodus from the land of Egypt, saying:


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
AND the Lord spoke to Moshe in the wilderness of Sinay, in the Tent of Meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they were come out of the land of Miżrayim, saying,


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses in the desert of Sinai in the tent of meeting on the first day of the second month (Iyyar) in the second year after their going out from the land of Egypt, saying:


###### Numbers 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/1:2)


שְׂא֗וּ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֙ כׇּל־עֲדַ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם לְבֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֑ם בְּמִסְפַּ֣ר שֵׁמ֔וֹת כׇּל־זָכָ֖ר לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Take a head count of the entire congregation of Bnei Yisroel according to their families to the house of their fathers counting the names of all males individually.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Yisra᾽el, after their families, by the houses of their fathers, by the number of names, every male by their polls;


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Take the count of the entire congregation of the children of Israel by their families [to know the number of each tribe], by their fathers' house [(one whose father is of one tribe and his mother of a different tribe being reckoned by the tribe of his father)], according to the number of names, every male by their heads [a beka (half a shekel) for a head (Exodus 38:26)].


###### Numbers 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/1:3)


מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה כׇּל־יֹצֵ֥א צָבָ֖א בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל תִּפְקְד֥וּ אֹתָ֛ם לְצִבְאֹתָ֖ם אַתָּ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Numbers 1:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/1:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/1:18)


וְאֵ֨ת כׇּל־הָעֵדָ֜ה הִקְהִ֗ילוּ בְּאֶחָד֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וַיִּתְיַֽלְד֥וּ עַל־מִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם לְבֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֑ם בְּמִסְפַּ֣ר שֵׁמ֗וֹת מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֛ה וָמַ֖עְלָה לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
They gathered together the entire congregation on the first [day] of the second month and they were registered by family ancestry according to the house of their fathers. according to the number of names each man of twenty years and above; individually.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the houses of their fathers, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, by their polls.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And they assembled the entire congregation on the first (day) of the second month, and they confirmed their birth (claims) [with deeds and witnesses] after their families, by their fathers' house, according to the number of names, (every male) from twenty years and up, by their heads [see 1].

###### Numbers 3:1

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

וְעַ֣ל**׀** מִזְבַּ֣ח הַזָּהָ֗ב יִפְרְשׂוּ֙ בֶּ֣גֶד תְּכֵ֔לֶת וְכִסּ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ בְּמִכְסֵ֖ה ע֣וֹר תָּ֑חַשׁ וְשָׂמ֖וּ אֶת־בַּדָּֽיו׃

On top of the golden Altar they shall spread a blue woolen cloth and they shall cover it with a covering of *tachash*-hide, and put its [carrying] poles in place.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
They shall put upon it all of its utensils which they use in service, those that are used on the Altar-top; the firepans, forks, scoops and sprinklers, all the utensils of the Altar. They shall spread upon it a covering of *tachash*-hide, and put its [carrying] poles in place.

###### Numbers 4:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/4:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/4:15)


וְכִלָּ֣ה אַֽהֲרֹן־וּ֠בָנָ֠יו לְכַסֹּ֨ת אֶת־הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ וְאֶת־כׇּל־כְּלֵ֣י הַקֹּ֘דֶשׁ֮ בִּנְסֹ֣עַ הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֒ וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן יָבֹ֤אוּ בְנֵי־קְהָת֙ לָשֵׂ֔את וְלֹֽא־יִגְּע֥וּ אֶל־הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ וָמֵ֑תוּ אֵ֛לֶּה מַשָּׂ֥א בְנֵֽי־קְהָ֖ת בְּאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Aharon and his sons shall complete the covering of the Sanctuary and all of the holy utensils whenever the camp is about to travel, and after that, the sons of Kehos shall come to carry [these items], and they shall not touch the Holy [objects] and they will [not] die. These are what the sons of Kehos must carry for the Tent of Meeting.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

These things are the burden of the sons of Qehat in the Tent of Meeting.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Aaron and his sons shall finish covering the holy (things) [the ark and the altar] and all the holy vessels when the camp is to travel, and then the sons of Kehath shall come to carry (them), and they shall not touch the holy (things) lest they die [(at the hands of Heaven)]. These (things) are the burden of the sons of Kehath in the tent of meeting.


###### Numbers 4:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/4:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/4:16)


וּפְקֻדַּ֞ת אֶלְעָזָ֣ר**׀** בֶּן־אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֗ן שֶׁ֤מֶן הַמָּאוֹר֙ וּקְטֹ֣רֶת הַסַּמִּ֔ים וּמִנְחַ֥ת הַתָּמִ֖יד וְשֶׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֑ה פְּקֻדַּ֗ת כׇּל־הַמִּשְׁכָּן֙ וְכׇל־אֲשֶׁר־בּ֔וֹ בְּקֹ֖דֶשׁ וּבְכֵלָֽיו׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Encharged to Elazar, the son of Aharon the *kohein,* is the oil for illumination, the incense of spices the continual [daily] meal-offering and the anointing oil; the charge of the entire *Mishkon* and all of its contents in the Sanctuary, and its utensils.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And to the office of El῾azar the son of Aharon the priest pertains the oil for the light, and the sweet incense, and the daily meal offering, and the anointing oil, and the oversight of all the tabernacle, and of all that is in it, as to the sanctuary, and as to its vessels.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

###### Numbers 5:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:8)

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:10)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

And when he has made her drink the water, then it shall come to pass, that, if she be defiled, and have done trespass against her husband, that the water that causes the curse shall enter into her, and become bitter, and her belly shall swell, and her thigh shall fall away: and the woman shall be a curse among her people.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And he shall make her drink the water [(to include an instance where she refused to drink after the scroll was blotted out; in which instance she is forcibly made to drink it — unless she admitted having been adulterous.)] And it shall be, if she had been defiled and had been faithless to her husband, then the blighting waters will enter her for bitterness, and her belly will swell and her thigh will fall. [Though in the curses (21) "thigh" precedes "belly," in operation, the waters first enter the belly and then the thigh.] And the woman will be a curse in the midst of her people.


###### Numbers 5:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:28)


וְאִם־לֹ֤א נִטְמְאָה֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּטְהֹרָ֖ה הִ֑וא וְנִקְּתָ֖ה וְנִזְרְעָ֥ה זָֽרַע׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
But if the woman was not defiled and [she] is pure, she will be cleansed and shall bear seed.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if the woman be not defiled, but be clean; then she shall be free, and shall conceive seed.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if the woman had not been defiled [in this concealment] and she be clean [of any other act], then she shall be absolved [of the blighting waters] and [what is more,] she will sow seed. [If she had difficult labors, she will have easy ones; if she had borne swarthy children, she will bear fair ones.]


###### Numbers 5:29

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:29)


זֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַקְּנָאֹ֑ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּשְׂטֶ֥ה אִשָּׁ֛ה תַּ֥חַת אִישָׁ֖הּ וְנִטְמָֽאָה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
This is the law of jealousies, when a woman goes astray during her marriage to her husband and is defiled.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
This is the Tora of jealousies, when a wife goes aside to another instead of her husband, and is defiled;


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
This is the law of the rancors for a woman who goes astray under her husband and is defiled.


###### Numbers 5:30

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:30](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:30)


א֣וֹ אִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תַּעֲבֹ֥ר עָלָ֛יו ר֥וּחַ קִנְאָ֖ה וְקִנֵּ֣א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְהֶעֱמִ֤יד אֶת־הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה וְעָ֤שָׂה לָהּ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֵ֥ת כׇּל־הַתּוֹרָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man is overcome with a spirit of jealousy and he is jealous of his wife, then he shall have the woman stand before Adonoy, and the *kohein* shall do unto her all of these laws.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
or when the spirit of jealousy comes upon him, and he be jealous of his wife, and shall set the woman before the Lord, and the priest shall execute upon her all this Tora:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If there pass over a man a spirit of rancor, then he shall warn his wife, and he shall stand his wife before the L-rd and the Cohein shall do with her all of this law.


###### Numbers 5:31

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:31](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/5:31)


וְנִקָּ֥ה הָאִ֖ישׁ מֵעָוֺ֑ן וְהָאִשָּׁ֣ה הַהִ֔וא תִּשָּׂ֖א אֶת־עֲוֺנָֽהּ׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The man is cleansed of sin and that woman shall bear [the burden of] her iniquity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
then shall the man be guiltless of iniquity, and this woman shall bear her iniquity.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the man will be free of sin [i.e., of liability for her death by the waters], and that woman shall bear her sin.



## Chapter 6

###### Numbers 6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:1)


וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהֹוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy spoke to Moshe, saying;


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord spoke to Moshe, saying,


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd spoke to Moses, saying:


###### Numbers 6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:2)


דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־אִשָּׁ֗ה כִּ֤י יַפְלִא֙ לִנְדֹּר֙ נֶ֣דֶר נָזִ֔יר לְהַזִּ֖יר לַֽיהֹוָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Speak to Bnei Yisroel and say to them: If a man or a woman sets apart a vow, a nazirite vow, to set [himself] apart for Adonoy.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Speak to the children of Yisra᾽el, and say to them, When either man or woman shall pronounce a special vow of a Nazir to separate themselves to the Lord:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: A man or a woman, if he utter a vow, the vow of a Nazirite [lit., "one who separates himself"] to separate himself [from wine] unto the L-rd [i.e., for the sake of Heaven], [(The rationale of the juxtaposition of verses — "All who witness a sotah (a woman suspected of infidelity) in her undoing should separate themselves from wine," wine inciting to licentiousness)],


###### Numbers 6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:3)


מִיַּ֤יִן וְשֵׁכָר֙ יַזִּ֔יר חֹ֥מֶץ יַ֛יִן וְחֹ֥מֶץ שֵׁכָ֖ר לֹ֣א יִשְׁתֶּ֑ה וְכׇל־מִשְׁרַ֤ת עֲנָבִים֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וַעֲנָבִ֛ים לַחִ֥ים וִיבֵשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א יֹאכֵֽל׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
From new or old [intoxicating] wine, he must abstain. Vinegar made from new wine and vinegar made from old wine he shall not drink; anything steeped in grapes he shall not drink; moist grapes or dried grapes (raisins) he shall not eat.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
he shall abstain from wine and strong drink, and shall drink no vinegar of wine, or vinegar of strong drink, nor shall he drink any liquor of grapes, nor eat moist grapes, or dried.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
From [new] wine and shechar [old (lit., "intoxicating") wine] he shall separate himself. Vinegar of wine and vinegar of shechar he shall not drink; and any steeping of grapes he shall not drink, and grapes, wet or dry, he shall not eat.


###### Numbers 6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:4)


כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֑וֹ מִכֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵעָשֶׂ֜ה מִגֶּ֣פֶן הַיַּ֗יִן מֵחַרְצַנִּ֛ים וְעַד־זָ֖ג לֹ֥א יֹאכֵֽל׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
As long as he is a *Nazir* from anything made of the grape-vine, from seeds to skin, he shall not eat.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All the days of his abstinence shall he eat nothing that is made of the vine tree, from the kernels even to the husk.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All the days of his Naziritism, of all that is made from the grapevine, from the kernels to the husk, he shall not eat.


###### Numbers 6:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:5)


כׇּל־יְמֵי֙ נֶ֣דֶר נִזְר֔וֹ תַּ֖עַר לֹא־יַעֲבֹ֣ר עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ עַד־מְלֹ֨את הַיָּמִ֜ם אֲשֶׁר־יַזִּ֤יר לַיהֹוָה֙ קָדֹ֣שׁ יִהְיֶ֔ה גַּדֵּ֥ל פֶּ֖רַע שְׂעַ֥ר רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
As long as he is under his nazirite oath a razor shall not pass over [to touch] his head. Until he completes his days as a *Nazir* to Adonoy he shall be sacred, he shall let the hair of his head grow long.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All the days of the vow of his separation there shall no razor come on his head: until the days are fulfilled, during which he separates himself to the Lord, he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All the days of the vow of his Naziritism a blade shall not pass over his head. Until the fulfillment of the days of his Naziritism to the L-rd, holy shall it [his hair] be [by his] letting grow long the growth [pera ("pera" is not less than thirty days)] of the hair of his head.


###### Numbers 6:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:6)


כׇּל־יְמֵ֥י הַזִּיר֖וֹ לַיהֹוָ֑ה עַל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ מֵ֖ת לֹ֥א יָבֹֽא׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
All the days that he is a *Nazir* to Adonoy, he shall have no contact with the dead.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All the days that he separates himself to the Lord he shall come at no dead body.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All the days of his Naziritism to the L-rd, by a dead body he shall not come.


###### Numbers 6:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:7)


לְאָבִ֣יו וּלְאִמּ֗וֹ לְאָחִיו֙ וּלְאַ֣חֹת֔וֹ לֹא־יִטַּמָּ֥א לָהֶ֖ם בְּמֹתָ֑ם כִּ֛י נֵ֥זֶר אֱלֹהָ֖יו עַל־רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
For his father, mother, brother and sister he shall not [ritually] defile himself for them when they die. For, the nazirite crown of his God is upon his head.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He shall not make himself unclean for his father, or for his mother, for his brother, or for his sister, when they die: because the crown of his God is upon his head.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, he shall not make himself unclean for them in their death, for the crown of his G-d is on his head.


###### Numbers 6:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:8)


כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֑וֹ קָדֹ֥שׁ ה֖וּא לַֽיהֹוָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
All the days of his separation, he is sacred to Adonoy.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All the days of his separation he is holy to the Lord.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All the days of his Naziritism, holy is he to the L-rd [("holiness" of body — not making himself unclean for the dead)].


###### Numbers 6:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:9)


וְכִֽי־יָמ֨וּת מֵ֤ת עָלָיו֙ בְּפֶ֣תַע פִּתְאֹ֔ם וְטִמֵּ֖א רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֑וֹ וְגִלַּ֤ח רֹאשׁוֹ֙ בְּי֣וֹם טׇהֳרָת֔וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י יְגַלְּחֶֽנּוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If someone died near him suddenly, or unexpectedly, and caused his nazirite crowned head to be defiled, he shall shave his head on the day of his purification, he shall shave it on the seventh day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if any man die very suddenly by him, and he has defiled the head of his consecration; then he shall shave his head in the day of his cleansing, on the seventh day shall he shave it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if any man die on him [in the tent where he finds himself], of an instant, unexpectedly, and he make unclean the head of his Naziritism, then he shall shave his head on the day of his cleansing [i.e., sprinkling (of the waters of the red heifer, 19:17)]; on the seventh day shall he shave it.


###### Numbers 6:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:10)


וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֗י יָבִא֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י תֹרִ֔ים א֥וֹ שְׁנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יוֹנָ֑ה אֶ֨ל־הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the *kohein,* to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtle doves, or two young pigeons, to the priest, to the door of the Tent of Meeting:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And on the eighth day [i.e., from the eighth day on], he shall bring two turtle-doves or two young pigeons to the Cohein, to the door of the tent of meeting.


###### Numbers 6:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:11)


וְעָשָׂ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן אֶחָ֤ד לְחַטָּאת֙ וְאֶחָ֣ד לְעֹלָ֔ה וְכִפֶּ֣ר עָלָ֔יו מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָ֖א עַל־הַנָּ֑פֶשׁ וְקִדַּ֥שׁ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The *kohein* shall prepare one for a sin-offering and one for a burnt-offering and atone on his behalf from his sin [of contact] with a [departed] soul, and he shall sanctify his head on that day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and the priest shall offer the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering, and make atonement for him, for that he sinned by the dead, and shall hallow his head that same day.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the Cohein shall offer one as a sin-offering and one as a burnt-offering, and he shall atone for him for having sinned through the (dead) body, and he shall hallow his head on that day [i.e., He shall begin again the count of his Naziritism].


###### Numbers 6:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:12)


וְהִזִּ֤יר לַֽיהֹוָה֙ אֶת־יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֔וֹ וְהֵבִ֛יא כֶּ֥בֶשׂ בֶּן־שְׁנָת֖וֹ לְאָשָׁ֑ם וְהַיָּמִ֤ים הָרִאשֹׁנִים֙ יִפְּל֔וּ כִּ֥י טָמֵ֖א נִזְרֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
He shall set apart, for Adonoy, his nazirite days, and bring a sheep in its first year as a guilt-offering. The first days shall elapse because his nazirite crown was defiled.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he shall consecrate to the Lord the days of his abstinence, and shall bring a lamb of the first year for a guilt offering: and the days that were before shall be lost, because his separation was defiled.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And he shall consecrate [anew] to the L-rd the days of his Naziritism, and he shall bring a lamb of the first year as a guilt-offering, and the first days shall fall off [from the count] because he made unclean his Naziritism.


###### Numbers 6:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:13)


וְזֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַנָּזִ֑יר בְּי֗וֹם מְלֹאת֙ יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֔וֹ יָבִ֣יא אֹת֔וֹ אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
This is the law of the *Nazir*: when the days of his nazirite status are fulfilled, he shall bring himself to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And this is the Tora of the Nazir, when the days of his separation are fulfilled: he shall be brought to the door of the Tent of Meeting.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And this is the law of the Nazirite. On the day of the fulfillment of the days of his Naziritism, he shall bring himself to the door of the tent of meeting.


###### Numbers 6:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:14)


וְהִקְרִ֣יב אֶת־קׇרְבָּנ֣וֹ לַיהֹוָ֡ה כֶּ֩בֶשׂ֩ בֶּן־שְׁנָת֨וֹ תָמִ֤ים אֶחָד֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה וְכַבְשָׂ֨ה אַחַ֧ת בַּת־שְׁנָתָ֛הּ תְּמִימָ֖ה לְחַטָּ֑את וְאַֽיִל־אֶחָ֥ד תָּמִ֖ים לִשְׁלָמִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
He shall bring his offering to Adonoy; one unblemished sheep, in its first year, as a burnt-offering, and one unblemished ewe, in its first year as a sin-offering, and one unblemished ram as a peace-offering.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he shall offer his offering to the Lord, one he lamb of the first year without blemish for a burnt offering, and one ewe lamb of the first year without blemish for a sin offering, and one ram without blemish for a peace offering,


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And he shall offer up his sacrifice to the L-rd: one lamb of the first year without blemish as a burnt-offering, and one ewe-lamb of the first year without blemish as a sin-offering, and one ram without blemish as a peace-offering.


###### Numbers 6:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:15)


וְסַ֣ל מַצּ֗וֹת סֹ֤לֶת חַלֹּת֙ בְּלוּלֹ֣ת בַּשֶּׁ֔מֶן וּרְקִיקֵ֥י מַצּ֖וֹת מְשֻׁחִ֣ים בַּשָּׁ֑מֶן וּמִנְחָתָ֖ם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
A basket of *matzos* of fine flour, loaves mixed with oil and *matzoh*-wafers spread with oil and their meal-offerings and libations.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and a basket of unleavened bread, cakes of fine flour mingled with oil, and wafers of unleavened bread anointed with oil, and their meal offering, and their drink offerings.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And a basket of unleavened bread of fine flour, [ten] cakes [of unleavened bread] mixed with oil, and [ten] wafers of unleavened bread smeared with oil, and their [the burnt-offering's and the peace-offering's] meal-offering and their drink-offerings.


###### Numbers 6:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:16)


וְהִקְרִ֥יב הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה וְעָשָׂ֥ה אֶת־חַטָּאת֖וֹ וְאֶת־עֹלָתֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The *kohein* shall bring it before Adonoy and do the service of his sin-offering and of his burnt-offering.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the priest shall bring them before the Lord, and shall offer his sin offering, and his burnt offering:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the Cohein shall present (them) before the L-rd, and he shall offer his sin-offering and his burnt-offering.


###### Numbers 6:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/6:17)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The *Nazir* shall shave—at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting—the nazirite crown of hair on his head, and he shall take the hair from the nazirite crown on his head and put it in the fire which is under the peace-offering sacrifice.

And he shall take the hair of the head of his Naziritism, and he shall place it on the fire under the sacrifice of the peace-offerings [i.e., under the cauldron (in the azarah) in which they are cooked (the Cohein being required to take the shoulder after it has been cooked and wave it before the L-rd)].

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The *kohein* shall take the cooked foreleg from the ram and one *matzoh*-loaf from the basket, and one *matzoh*-wafer, and put it on the palms of the *Nazir* after he has shaved his nazirite crown.

זֹ֣את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַנָּזִיר֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדֹּר֒ קׇרְבָּנ֤וֹ לַֽיהֹוָה֙ עַל־נִזְר֔וֹ מִלְּבַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר־תַּשִּׂ֣יג יָד֑וֹ כְּפִ֤י נִדְרוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדֹּ֔ר כֵּ֣ן יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה עַ֖ל תּוֹרַ֥ת נִזְרֽוֹ׃{פ}

This is the law of the Nazirite who shall vow his offering to the L-rd for his Naziritism, aside from what his hand attains [i.e., if he vows more than the prescribed number of offerings, he must bring them.] According to the vow that he vows, thus shall he do above [(but not below)] the law of his Naziriteship [i.e., the prescribed number of offerings].

## Chapter 7

###### Numbers 7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:1)


וַיְהִ֡י בְּיוֹם֩ כַּלּ֨וֹת מֹשֶׁ֜ה לְהָקִ֣ים אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֗ן וַיִּמְשַׁ֨ח אֹת֜וֹ וַיְקַדֵּ֤שׁ אֹתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־כׇּל־כֵּלָ֔יו וְאֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וְאֶת־כׇּל־כֵּלָ֑יו וַיִּמְשָׁחֵ֖ם וַיְקַדֵּ֥שׁ אֹתָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
It came to pass, on the day Moshe finished erecting the *Mishkon,* and he anointed it and consecrated it and all of its utensils, and the Altar and all its utensils, and he anointed them and consecrated them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And it came to pass on the day that Moshe had finished setting up the tabernacle, and had anointed it, and sanctified it, and all its instruments, both the altar and all its vessels, and had anointed them, and sanctified them;


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And it was, on the day that Moses had finished (kalloth) setting up the mishkan and had anointed it and consecrated it and all of its vessels, and (he had set up) the altar and all of its vessels, and had anointed them and consecrated them, [(kalloth): On the day of the setting up of the mishkan, Israel was like a bride (kallah) entering the bridal canopy. ("that Moses had finished"): Although Betzalel and other craftsmen had made the mishkan, it is attributed to Moses for having given heart and soul to see to it that the last detail was executed exactly as the L-rd had revealed it to him on Mount Sinai. ("on the day that Moses had finished setting up"): All of the seven days of the investiture, Moses would assemble and dismantle the mishkan, and it was on the eighth day that he assembled it and did not dismantle it. ("On the day that Moses had finished setting up the mishkan"): It was Rosh Chodesh Nissan. On the second (of Nissan) the red heifer was burned; on the third, the first sprinkling (of the cleansing waters) took place, and on the seventh day (the Levites) shaved (see 8:6)],

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:2)


וַיַּקְרִ֙יבוּ֙ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רָאשֵׁ֖י בֵּ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֑ם הֵ֚ם נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הַמַּטֹּ֔ת הֵ֥ם הָעֹמְדִ֖ים עַל־הַפְּקֻדִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The leaders of Israel brought, [those who were] the heads of their fathers’ houses; they were the leaders of the tribes, they stood by during the counting.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
that the princes of Yisra᾽el, heads of the house of their fathers, who were the princes of the tribes, and were over them that were numbered, offered:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
That the chiefs of Israel, the heads of their fathers' house, the chiefs of the tribes, [who were their overseers in Egypt, and who were smitten because of them (Exodus 5:14)], they who stood [with Moses and Aaron] over the ones who were numbered [(1:4)], presented (their offerings).


###### Numbers 7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:3)


וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ אֶת־קׇרְבָּנָ֜ם לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֗ה שֵׁשׁ־עֶגְלֹ֥ת צָב֙ וּשְׁנֵ֣י עָשָׂ֣ר בָּקָ֔ר עֲגָלָ֛ה עַל־שְׁנֵ֥י הַנְּשִׂאִ֖ים וְשׁ֣וֹר לְאֶחָ֑ד וַיַּקְרִ֥יבוּ אוֹתָ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃

They brought their offerings before Adonoy; six covered wagons and twelve oxen; a wagon for each two leaders and an ox for each individual, and they placed them before the *Mishkon.*

and they brought their offering before the Lord, six covered wagons, and twelve oxen; a wagon for every two of the princes, and for each one an ox: and they brought them before the tabernacle.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And they brought their offerings before the L-rd, six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon for every two chiefs, and an ox for each, and they presented them before the mishkan [(Moses did not take it from their hands until the L-rd told him to do so)].

Adonoy said to Moshe, saying:


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord spoke to Moshe, saying,

And the L-rd said to Moses, saying:

קַ֚ח מֵֽאִתָּ֔ם וְהָי֕וּ לַעֲבֹ֕ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֖ת אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְנָתַתָּ֤ה אוֹתָם֙ אֶל־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִ֥י עֲבֹדָתֽוֹ׃

###### Numbers 7:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:10)


וַיַּקְרִ֣יבוּ הַנְּשִׂאִ֗ים אֵ֚ת חֲנֻכַּ֣ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ בְּי֖וֹם הִמָּשַׁ֣ח אֹת֑וֹ וַיַּקְרִ֧יבוּ הַנְּשִׂיאִ֛ם אֶת־קׇרְבָּנָ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The leaders brought forward the [offerings for] the consecration of the altar on the day it was anointed. The leaders placed their offering before the altar.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the princes offered for dedicating of the altar in the day that it was anointed, and the princes offered their offering before the altar.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the chiefs presented the inauguration (offerings) of the altar on the day it was anointed [(After they had donated the wagons and the oxen for bearing the wagons, their hearts moved them to donate offerings for the inauguration of the altar)], and the chiefs presented their offerings before the altar. [Moses did not take them from their hands until the L-rd told him to do so.]


###### Numbers 7:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:11)


וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהֹוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה נָשִׂ֨יא אֶחָ֜ד לַיּ֗וֹם נָשִׂ֤יא אֶחָד֙ לַיּ֔וֹם יַקְרִ֙יבוּ֙ אֶת־קׇרְבָּנָ֔ם לַחֲנֻכַּ֖ת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe: One leader each day, one leader each day, they shall bring forth their offering, for the dedication of the altar.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord said to Moshe, They shall offer their offering, each prince on his day, for the dedicating of the altar.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses: Each chief on his day, each chief on his day, shall present his offerings for the inauguration of the altar. [And Moses did not know whether to follow the order of birth or the order of traveling (see section 2), until the L-rd told him to follow the order of traveling.]


###### Numbers 7:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:12)


וַיְהִ֗י הַמַּקְרִ֛יב בַּיּ֥וֹם הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן אֶת־קׇרְבָּנ֑וֹ נַחְשׁ֥וֹן בֶּן־עַמִּינָדָ֖ב לְמַטֵּ֥ה יְהוּדָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The one that brought his offering on the first day [was] Nachshon the son of Aminadav, of the tribe of Yehudah.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he that offered his offering the first day was Naĥshon the son of ῾Amminadav, of the tribe of Yehuda:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the one who presented his offering on the first day was Nachshon ben Aminadav of the tribe of Judah.


###### Numbers 7:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:13)


וְקׇרְבָּנ֞וֹ קַֽעֲרַת־כֶּ֣סֶף אַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וּמֵאָה֮ מִשְׁקָלָהּ֒ מִזְרָ֤ק אֶחָד֙ כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁבְעִ֥ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ שְׁנֵיהֶ֣ם**׀** מְלֵאִ֗ים סֹ֛לֶת בְּלוּלָ֥ה בַשֶּׁ֖מֶן לְמִנְחָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
His offering was one silver tray, its weight was one hundred thirty *shekolim;* one silver bowl [that weighed] seventy *shekolim* according to sanctuary weights. Both were filled with fine flour kneaded with [olive] oil, for a meal-offering.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and his offering was one silver dish, the weight of which was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them were full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal offering:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And his offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels in the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a [donative] meal-offering.


###### Numbers 7:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/7:14)


כַּ֥ף אַחַ֛ת עֲשָׂרָ֥ה זָהָ֖ב מְלֵאָ֥ה קְטֹֽרֶת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
One spoon of ten gold [*shekolim*], filled with incense.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
one spoon of ten shekels of gold, full of incense:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
One spoon, [weighing] ten gold [shekels], full of incense [This is the only instance of incense offered by an individual, and on the outer altar — a "one-time ruling"]

Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you kindle the lamps (of the menorah), towards the face [the central shaft] of the menorah shall the seven lamps light [i.e., shall their light (by manipulation of the wicks) be directed (so that people not say that He needs the menorah for its light)].

and Aharon shall offer the Levites before the Lord for an offering of the children of Yisra᾽el, that they may execute the service of the Lord.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Aaron shall wave the Levites, a waving before the L-rd, [just as the guilt-offering of the leper required waving live (Leviticus 14:12)] from the children of Israel, and they shall serve the service of the L-rd. [Three "wavings" are mentioned in this section. This first applies to the sons of Kehath, upon whom the service of the holy of holies devolved (i.e., the bearing of the ark, the table, etc.) — thus: "and they shall serve the service of the L-rd."]

## Chapter 9

###### Numbers 9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/9:1)


וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהֹוָ֣ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה בְמִדְבַּר־סִ֠ינַ֠י בַּשָּׁנָ֨ה הַשֵּׁנִ֜ית לְצֵאתָ֨ם מֵאֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן לֵאמֹֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy spoke to Moshe in the desert of Sinai in the second year of their exodus from the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying;


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord spoke to Moshe in the wilderness of Sinay, in the first month of the second year after they were come out of the land of Miżrayim, saying,


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai in the second year after their going out from the land of Egypt, in the first month (Nissan), saying: [(Bamidbar begins with the second month (1:1) — whence it is derived that "there is no before and after (i.e., strict chronological sequence) in the Torah." (It does not begin with this section for it is disparaging to Israel that all the forty years that they were in the desert they offered only this one Paschal sacrifice.)]


###### Numbers 9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/9:2)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Bnei Yisroel shall perform the *Pesach*-offering in its proper time.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Let the children of Yisra᾽el also keep the passover at its appointed season.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The children of Israel shall offer the Pesach in its appointed time, [even on the Sabbath, even in a state of (communal) uncleanliness].


###### Numbers 9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/9:3)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
On the fourteenth day of this month, in the afternoon, you shall perform it in its proper time; according to all its statutes and according to all its laws you shall perform it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
On the fourteenth day of this month, towards evening shall you offer it, in its appointed time. According to all of its statutes [the mitzvoth relating directly to its body] and according to all its [attendant] ordinances shall you offer it.


###### Numbers 9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/9:4)


וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַעֲשֹׂ֥ת הַפָּֽסַח׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

## Chapter 11

###### Numbers 11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:1)


וַיְהִ֤י הָעָם֙ כְּמִתְאֹ֣נְנִ֔ים רַ֖ע בְּאׇזְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהֹוָה֙ וַיִּ֣חַר אַפּ֔וֹ וַתִּבְעַר־בָּם֙ אֵ֣שׁ יְהֹוָ֔ה וַתֹּ֖אכַל בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The people were like complainers; [it was] wicked in the ears of Adonoy. Adonoy heard and His Anger flared and the fire of Adonoy burned among them and consumed [some] of the outcasts of the camp.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And when the people complained, it displeased the Lord: and the Lord heard it; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the Lord burned among them, and consumed those who were in the uttermost parts of the camp.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the people, [the wicked ones,] were as seekers of a pretext [to forsake Him], that was evil in the ears of the L-rd [i.e., that would antagonize Him when it reached His ears and would provoke Him. They said: "Woe unto us — how this three-days journey has wearied us!"] And the L-rd heard and His wrath was kindled [(He said:) I did this for your own good, so that you would enter the land immediately! (see 10:33)], and the fire of the L-rd burned in them, and it devoured in the "end" of the camp [i.e., the lowest among them, the eirav rav (the mixed multitude)].


###### Numbers 11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:2)


וַיִּצְעַ֥ק הָעָ֖ם אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה וַתִּשְׁקַ֖ע הָאֵֽשׁ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The people cried out to Moshe, and Moshe prayed to Adonoy, and the fire subsided.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the people cried out to Moses [to intercede for them], and Moses prayed to the L-rd, and the fire sank [in its place, into the earth. (Had it retreated, it would have consumed that area.)]


###### Numbers 11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:3)


וַיִּקְרָ֛א שֵֽׁם־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא תַּבְעֵרָ֑ה כִּֽי־בָעֲרָ֥ה בָ֖ם אֵ֥שׁ יְהֹוָֽה׃

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Numbers 11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:4)


וְהָֽאסַפְסֻף֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ הִתְאַוּ֖וּ תַּאֲוָ֑ה וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ וַיִּבְכּ֗וּ גַּ֚ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֥י יַאֲכִלֵ֖נוּ בָּשָֽׂר׃

The collection [of nationalities] among them began to have strong cravings, and Bnei Yisroel turned and began to weep; and they said “Who will feed us meat?

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

[(They had flesh [see Exodus 12:38 and Numbers 32:1] — they were only seeking a pretext)].


###### Numbers 11:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:5)


זָכַ֙רְנוּ֙ אֶת־הַדָּגָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נֹאכַ֥ל בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם חִנָּ֑ם אֵ֣ת הַקִּשֻּׁאִ֗ים וְאֵת֙ הָֽאֲבַטִּחִ֔ים וְאֶת־הֶחָצִ֥יר וְאֶת־הַבְּצָלִ֖ים וְאֶת־הַשּׁוּמִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
We remember the fish which we ate in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, watermelons, leeks, onions and garlic.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
We remember the fish, which we did eat in Miżrayim for nothing; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
We remember the fish that we would eat in Egypt, free [of mitzvoth], the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic. [The (flavor of the) manna would change into any (flavor they desired) except these, for they are harmful to nursing women.]


###### Numbers 11:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:6)


וְעַתָּ֛ה נַפְשֵׁ֥נוּ יְבֵשָׁ֖ה אֵ֣ין כֹּ֑ל בִּלְתִּ֖י אֶל־הַמָּ֥ן עֵינֵֽינוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Now our bodies are withered, there is nothing at all, but the manna before our eyes.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
but now our soul is dried away: there is nothing at all, beside this manna, before our eyes.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Numbers 11:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:7)


וְהַמָּ֕ן כִּזְרַע־גַּ֖ד ה֑וּא וְעֵינ֖וֹ כְּעֵ֥ין הַבְּדֹֽלַח׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The manna was like coriander seed and it is similiar to the appearance of crystal.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the manna was like coriander seed, and its colour was like the colour of bdellium.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[What follows is an "interjection" by the Holy One Blessed be He, viz.: See what My children are railing against!] The manna was [round] like coriander seed, and it looked like crystal.

שָׁ֩טוּ֩ הָעָ֨ם וְלָֽקְט֜וּ וְטָחֲנ֣וּ בָרֵחַ֗יִם א֤וֹ דָכוּ֙ בַּמְּדֹכָ֔ה וּבִשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּפָּר֔וּר וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ עֻג֑וֹת וְהָיָ֣ה טַעְמ֔וֹ כְּטַ֖עַם לְשַׁ֥ד הַשָּֽׁמֶן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The people [merely] strolled about and they gathered it and they ground it with a millstone or crushed it in mortars and cooked it in pots and made cakes out of it. Its taste was like the taste of cake kneaded with oil.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the people went about, and gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in a mortar, and boiled it in a pot, and made cakes of it: and the taste of it was like the taste of oil cake.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The people would stroll out and gather it [effortlessly], and they would grind it in a mill, or beat it in a mortar, or cook it in a pot [i.e., they could make it taste as if it had been ground in a mill, etc.], and they made cakes of it; and its taste was like the "sap" of oil.

When the dew would descend on the camp, at night, the manna would descend on it.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־הָעָ֗ם בֹּכֶה֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔יו אִ֖ישׁ לְפֶ֣תַח אׇהֳל֑וֹ וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֤ף יְהֹוָה֙ מְאֹ֔ד וּבְעֵינֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה רָֽע׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe heard the people weep according to their families, at the door of each one’s tent. The Anger of Adonoy was greatly aroused and in Moshe’s eyes, it was evil.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe heard the people weeping throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent: and the anger of the Lord burned greatly; Moshe also was displeased.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses heard the people weeping by its families, [who gathered together to air their plaints], each at the door of his tent. And the L-rd was extremely wroth, and in the eyes of Moses it was evil.

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־יְהֹוָ֗ה לָמָ֤ה הֲרֵעֹ֙תָ֙ לְעַבְדֶּ֔ךָ וְלָ֛מָּה לֹא־מָצָ֥תִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ לָשׂ֗וּם אֶת־מַשָּׂ֛א כׇּל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה עָלָֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe said to Adonoy: “Why have you dealt poorly with Your servant, and why have I not found favor in Your eyes that You place the burden of the entire people upon me?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe said to the Lord, Why hast thou afflicted thy servant? and why have I not found favour in thy sight, that thou layst the burden of all this people upon me?


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses said to the L-rd: Why have You done evil to Your servant, and why have I not found favor in Your eyes, to place the burden of all this people upon me!


###### Numbers 11:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:12)


הֶאָנֹכִ֣י הָרִ֗יתִי אֵ֚ת כׇּל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אִם־אָנֹכִ֖י יְלִדְתִּ֑יהוּ כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֨ר אֵלַ֜י שָׂאֵ֣הוּ בְחֵיקֶ֗ךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשָּׂ֤א הָאֹמֵן֙ אֶת־הַיֹּנֵ֔ק עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתָּ לַאֲבֹתָֽיו׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Have I conceived this entire people? have I given birth to it that You say to me, carry it in your lap as a nurse carries an infant, to the land which You swore to their forefathers?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Have I conceived all this people? have I begotten them, that thou shouldst say to me, Carry them in thy bosom, as a nursing father carries the sucking child, to the land which thou hast sworn to their fathers?


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Did I conceive all this people? Did I beget them, that You say to me: Bear them in your bosom, as a nurse bears a nursling, to the land which You promised to their fathers? [see Exodus 32:34 and 6:13].

From where do I have meat to give to this entire people on account of which they cry to me, saying: “Give us meat and we shall eat.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Whence should I have meat to give to all this people? for they weep to me, saying, Give us meat, that we may eat.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Whence am I to take flesh to give to all this people? For they weep over me, saying: Give us flesh and let us eat!

I alone can not carry this entire people, for they are too burdensome for me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I shall not be able to bear alone all this people, for it is beyond my strength.


###### Numbers 11:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:15)


וְאִם־כָּ֣כָה**׀** אַתְּ־עֹ֣שֶׂה לִּ֗י הׇרְגֵ֤נִי נָא֙ הָרֹ֔ג אִם־מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וְאַל־אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּרָעָתִֽי׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If this is the way You treat me, please kill me, if I have found favor in Your eyes; so that I will not see my evil.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight: and let me not see my own wretchedness.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if thus [You will do to them (The L-rd showed Moses the calamity that He was going to bring upon them)], You are rendering me "at" [(a term for the feminine), Moses' strength waning as that of a woman]. Kill me, I pray You, if I have found favor in Your eyes, and let me not witness my [(a "euphemism" for "their")] evil.


###### Numbers 11:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:16)


וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֶסְפָה־לִּ֞י שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִישׁ֮ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּי־הֵ֛ם זִקְנֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם וְשֹׁטְרָ֑יו וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ אֹתָם֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֥וּ שָׁ֖ם עִמָּֽךְ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe: “Gather seventy men for Me, from among the elders of Israel, [men] whom you know to be the people’s elders, and its officers, and you shall take them to the Tent of Meeting, and they shall stand there with you.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord said to Moshe, Gather to me seventy men of the elders of Yisra᾽el, whom thou knowst to be the elders of the people, and officers over them; and bring them to the Tent of Meeting, that they may stand there with thee.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses [Here is My response to your "I shall not be able to bear alone"]: Gather unto Me seventy men from the elders of Israel [(The original elders had been killed at Taveirah in delayed retribution for their sin [see Exodus 24:11] (delayed so as not to dampen the joy of the giving of the Torah)], whom you know to be the elders of the people and its officers, [who were appointed over them in Egypt (Since they pitied them and were smitten by the Egyptians because of them, it is only fitting that they be raised in Israel's greatness as they shared in its woes.)], and take them to the tent of meeting, and have them stand there with you, [so that the people see, and accord them honor, saying: How beloved these must be, who entered with Moses to hear the Word from the mouth of the Holy One Blessed be He!]


###### Numbers 11:17

וְיָרַדְתִּ֗י וְדִבַּרְתִּ֣י עִמְּךָ֮ שָׁם֒ וְאָצַלְתִּ֗י מִן־הָר֛וּחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְנָשְׂא֤וּ אִתְּךָ֙ בְּמַשָּׂ֣א הָעָ֔ם וְלֹא־תִשָּׂ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
I will descend and speak there with you, and I will make greater the spirit which is upon you, and place it on them, and they will bear, along with you, the burden of the people so that you need not bear it alone.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee that thou bear it not thyself alone.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I shall go down and speak with you, [but not with them,] there. And I shall increase, from the spirit which is upon you, and I will place it upon them, [as all take light from a lamp on a menorah, without that lamp losing any of its own light.] And they shall bear with you the burden of the people [Stipulate with them: (This grandeur is being accorded them) on condition that they take upon themselves the wardship of My children, who are troublesome and refractory], and you shall not bear alone. [Thus, the response to "I shall not be able to bear alone."]

וְאֶל־הָעָ֨ם תֹּאמַ֜ר הִתְקַדְּשׁ֣וּ לְמָחָר֮ וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֣ם בָּשָׂר֒ כִּ֡י בְּכִיתֶם֩ בְּאׇזְנֵ֨י יְהֹוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֤י יַאֲכִלֵ֙נוּ֙ בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּי־ט֥וֹב לָ֖נוּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְנָתַ֨ן יְהֹוָ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם בָּשָׂ֖ר וַאֲכַלְתֶּֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall say to the people, prepare yourselves for the morrow and you shall eat meat, for you have cried in the ears of Adonoy, saying: “Who will feed us meat; we had it good in Egypt;” [now] Adonoy gives you meat and you shall eat.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And say to the people, Sanctify yourselves against tomorrow, and you shall eat meat: for you have wept in the ears of the Lord, saying, Who shall give us meat to eat? for it was well with us in Miżrayim: therefore the Lord will give you meat, and you shall eat.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And to the people shall you say: Prepare yourselves for [retribution] tomorrow, and you shall eat flesh. For you have wept in the ears of the L-rd, saying: Who shall feed us flesh? For it was good for us in Egypt. And the L-rd shall give you flesh and you shall eat.

לֹ֣א י֥וֹם אֶחָ֛ד תֹּאכְל֖וּן וְלֹ֣א יוֹמָ֑יִם וְלֹ֣א**׀** חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה יָמִ֗ים וְלֹא֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה יָמִ֔ים וְלֹ֖א עֶשְׂרִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃

Not for one day will you be eating and not for two days; not for five days, not for ten days, and not for twenty days.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Not one day shall you eat, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days;


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Not one day shall you eat, and not two days, and not five days, and not ten days, and not twenty days.


###### Numbers 11:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:20)


עַ֣ד**׀** חֹ֣דֶשׁ יָמִ֗ים עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵא֙ מֵֽאַפְּכֶ֔ם וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לְזָרָ֑א יַ֗עַן כִּֽי־מְאַסְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־יְהֹוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֔ם וַתִּבְכּ֤וּ לְפָנָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה יָצָ֥אנוּ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
But rather for a month of days, until it comes out of your nostrils and it will be repulsive to you; [this is] because you have rejected Adonoy Who is among you, and you have cried before Him, saying: “Why have we come out from Egypt?”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
but a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils, and it be loathsome to you: because you have despised the Lord who is among you, and have wept before him, saying, Why did we come out of Miżrayim?


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Until a month of days [(this, with the less wicked, who languished in their beds and their souls expired, see 33)], until it comes out of your nostrils [i.e., until it becomes loathsome to you], and it will be rejected by you [more than you sought it]. For you have despised the L-rd who is in your midst [(Had I not reposed My shechinah among you, your hearts would not have been "inflated" unto all these things)], and you have wept before Him, saying: Why, now, did we leave Egypt!


###### Numbers 11:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:21)


וַיֹּ֘אמֶר֮ מֹשֶׁה֒ שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֙לֶף֙ רַגְלִ֔י הָעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ וְאַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֗רְתָּ בָּשָׂר֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם וְאָכְל֖וּ חֹ֥דֶשׁ יָמִֽים׃

Moshe said: “The people are six hundred thousand on foot that I am among and You say that I will give them meat, to eat it for a month of days?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe said, The people, among whom I am, are six hundred thousand footmen; and thou hast said, I will give them meat, that they may eat a whole month.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses said: Six hundred thousand foot are the people in whose midst I am, and You say: Meat shall I give to them, and they shall eat a month of days!


###### Numbers 11:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:22)


הֲצֹ֧אן וּבָקָ֛ר יִשָּׁחֵ֥ט לָהֶ֖ם וּמָצָ֣א לָהֶ֑ם אִ֣ם אֶֽת־כׇּל־דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֛ם יֵאָסֵ֥ף לָהֶ֖ם וּמָצָ֥א לָהֶֽם׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Will sheep and cattle be slaughtered for them would that be sufficient for them? If all the fish of the sea would be gathered for them, would that be sufficient for them?”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Shall flocks and herds be slain for them, to suffice them? or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to suffice them?


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If flocks and herds are slaughtered for them, will it be sufficient for them! If all the fish of the sea are gathered for them, will it be sufficient for them! [i.e., even if You give them what they ask, they will not be satisfied, for they are simply seeking a pretext against You.]


###### Numbers 11:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:23)


וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה הֲיַ֥ד יְהֹוָ֖ה תִּקְצָ֑ר עַתָּ֥ה תִרְאֶ֛ה הֲיִקְרְךָ֥ דְבָרִ֖י אִם־לֹֽא׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe: “Has the Hand of Adonoy become short ? Now you will see if My words will occur unto you or not.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord said to Moshe, Is the Lord’s hand too short? thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass to thee or not.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses: Shall the hand of the L-rd be found wanting? [i.e., If I do not give it, they will call My omnipotence into question. At this, Moses said: Let me go and attempt to conciliate them — whereupon the L-rd said:] Now You will see whether My word [that they will not heed you] will befall you or not.


###### Numbers 11:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:24)


וַיֵּצֵ֣א מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיְדַבֵּר֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה וַיֶּאֱסֹ֞ף שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲמֵ֥ד אֹתָ֖ם סְבִיבֹ֥ת הָאֹֽהֶל׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe went out and spoke the words of Adonoy to the people, and he gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and he had them stand around the Tent.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe went out, and told the people the words of the Lord, and gathered seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the tent.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses went out and told the people the words of the L-rd, [viz.: "Shall the hand of the L-rd be found wanting?" Did He not give you water from the rock, etc.? (but they did not heed him and denied G-d's ability to satisfy their present need)]; and, [seeing that he was not being heeded], he gathered seventy men from the elders of the people, and he stood them roundabout the tent.


###### Numbers 11:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:25)


וַיֵּ֨רֶד יְהֹוָ֥ה׀בֶּעָנָן֮ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָיו֒ וַיָּ֗אצֶל מִן־הָר֙וּחַ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו וַיִּתֵּ֕ן עַל־שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ הַזְּקֵנִ֑ים וַיְהִ֗י כְּנ֤וֹחַ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ הָר֔וּחַ וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ וְלֹ֥א יָסָֽפוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy descended in a cloud and spoke to him, and He magnified the spirit which was upon him and He gave it unto the seventy men, [who were] the elders. When the spirit came to rest upon them they prophesied, and they did not cease.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord came down in a cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it to the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, but continued not.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd descended in a cloud and He spoke to him, and He increased from the spirit which was upon him [see 17], and He placed it upon the seventy men, the elders. And it was, when the spirit rested upon them, that they prophesied — but [after that day], they prophesied no more.


###### Numbers 11:26

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:26](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:26)


וַיִּשָּׁאֲר֣וּ שְׁנֵֽי־אֲנָשִׁ֣ים׀בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֡ה שֵׁ֣ם הָאֶחָ֣ד׀אֶלְדָּ֡ד וְשֵׁם֩ הַשֵּׁנִ֨י מֵידָ֜ד וַתָּ֧נַח עֲלֵהֶ֣ם הָר֗וּחַ וְהֵ֙מָּה֙ בַּכְּתֻבִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָצְא֖וּ הָאֹ֑הֱלָה וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Two people remained in the camp; one’s name was Eldad and the second one’s name was Meidad. The spirit rested upon them; they were among those inscribed, and they did not go out to the Tent, and they prophesied in the camp.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And there remained two of the men in the camp, the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the spirit rested upon them; and they were of them that were written, but went not out to the tent: and they prophesied in the camp.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And there remained two men [of those who had been chosen as elders] in the camp, the name of the one, Eldad; the name of the other, Medad, and the spirit rested upon them. And they were among those [designated as "elders"] on the ballots, but they did not go out to the tent, [saying: We are not worthy of this greatness], and they prophesied in the camp.


###### Numbers 11:27

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:27](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:27)


וַיָּ֣רׇץ הַנַּ֔עַר וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לְמֹשֶׁ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֶלְדָּ֣ד וּמֵידָ֔ד מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֖ים בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The youth ran and told Moshe, and said: “Eldad and Meidad are prophesying in the camp.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And there ran a young man, and told Moshe, and said, Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the youth [(some say it was Gershon, the son of Moses)] ran, and told Moses, saying: Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.


###### Numbers 11:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:28)


וַיַּ֜עַן יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־נ֗וּן מְשָׁרֵ֥ת מֹשֶׁ֛ה מִבְּחֻרָ֖יו וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנִ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה כְּלָאֵֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Yehoshua the son of Nun answered, [he being] the attendant of Moshe, from his youth, and he said: “My master Moshe, destroy them!”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Yehoshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moshe from his youth, answered and said, My lord Moshe restrain them.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses from his youth, responded and said: My Lord Moses, cause them to cease [from prophesying ("Saddle them" with community service and they will cease prophesying of themselves.)]


###### Numbers 11:29

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:29)


וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה הַֽמְקַנֵּ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לִ֑י וּמִ֨י יִתֵּ֜ן כׇּל־עַ֤ם יְהֹוָה֙ נְבִיאִ֔ים כִּי־יִתֵּ֧ן יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־רוּח֖וֹ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe said to him, “Are you vengeful for me? Would (that) it be that all Adonoy’s people were prophets, that Adonoy would give His Spirit upon them.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe said to him, Enviest thou for my sake? would that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them!


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses said to him: Are you zealous for my sake? Would that all the L-rd's people were prophets, that the L-rd would place His spirit upon them!


###### Numbers 11:30

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:30](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:30)


וַיֵּאָסֵ֥ף מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה ה֖וּא וְזִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe entered into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe retired into the camp, he and the elders of Yisra᾽el.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses retired [from the tent of meeting] into [his tent in] the camp, he and the elders of Israel. [(The L-rd did not punish Israel until each one of the righteous had entered his tent)].


###### Numbers 11:31

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:31](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:31)


וְר֜וּחַ נָסַ֣ע**׀** מֵאֵ֣ת יְהֹוָ֗ה וַיָּ֣גׇז שַׂלְוִים֮ מִן־הַיָּם֒ וַיִּטֹּ֨שׁ עַל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֜ה כְּדֶ֧רֶךְ י֣וֹם כֹּ֗ה וּכְדֶ֤רֶךְ יוֹם֙ כֹּ֔ה סְבִיב֖וֹת הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וּכְאַמָּתַ֖יִם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
From Adonoy there gusted a wind and He caused quail to fly from the sea and spread them over the camp, about a day’s journey from this side and about a day’s journey from that side, around the camp, and about two *amo¯s* above the ground’s surface.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And a wind went out from the Lord, and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, about a day’s journey on this side, and about a day’s journey on the other side, round about the camp, and about two cubits high upon the face of the earth.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And a wind went forth from the L-rd and "flew in" quail from the sea, and it spread over the camp, about a day's journey on one side and a day's journey on the other, roundabout the camp, and about two cubits above the face of the earth. [They hovered chest-high so that they could be easily gathered in.]


###### Numbers 11:32

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:32](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:32)


וַיָּ֣קׇם הָעָ֡ם כׇּל־הַיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא וְכׇל־הַלַּ֜יְלָה וְכֹ֣ל**׀** י֣וֹם הַֽמׇּחֳרָ֗ת וַיַּֽאַסְפוּ֙ אֶת־הַשְּׂלָ֔ו הַמַּמְעִ֕יט אָסַ֖ף עֲשָׂרָ֣ה חֳמָרִ֑ים וַיִּשְׁטְח֤וּ לָהֶם֙ שָׁט֔וֹחַ סְבִיב֖וֹת הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The people arose all of that day, the entire night and the entire next day, and they gathered the quail. He who gathered the least amount, gathered ten heaps and they spread them for themselves around the camp.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the people stood up all that day, and all that night, and all the next day, and they gathered the quails: he that gathered least gathered a quantity of ten ĥomer: and they spread them all abroad for themselves round about the camp.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the people rose all that day and all the night, and all the next day, and they gathered the quail. He that gathered least, [the indolent and the lame], gathered ten chamarim (homers), and they spread them in layers roundabout the camp.


###### Numbers 11:33

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:33](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:33)


הַבָּשָׂ֗ר עוֹדֶ֙נּוּ֙ בֵּ֣ין שִׁנֵּיהֶ֔ם טֶ֖רֶם יִכָּרֵ֑ת וְאַ֤ף יְהֹוָה֙ חָרָ֣ה בָעָ֔ם וַיַּ֤ךְ יְהֹוָה֙ בָּעָ֔ם מַכָּ֖ה רַבָּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The meat was still between their teeth before it was [even] finished, when the wrath of Adonoy was incited upon the people, and Adonoy smote the people an enormous blow.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And while the meat was yet between their teeth, before it was chewed, the wrath of the Lord was inflamed against the people, and the Lord smote the people with a very great plague.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The flesh was yet between their teeth [(this, with the wicked, see 10)], not yet consumed, when the wrath of the L-rd burned against the people; and the L-rd smote the people with a very great plague.


###### Numbers 11:34

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:34](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:34)


וַיִּקְרָ֛א אֶת־שֵֽׁם־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא קִבְר֣וֹת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֑ה כִּי־שָׁם֙ קָֽבְר֔וּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם הַמִּתְאַוִּֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
He called the name of that place Kivros Hataavoh, for it was there that they buried the people who had these cravings.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he called the name of that place Qivrot-hatta᾽ava (Graves of Lust): because there they buried the people that lusted.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And he called the name of that place Kivroth Hata'avah ("the graves of the lust"); for there they buried the people that lusted.


###### Numbers 11:35

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:35](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/11:35)


מִקִּבְר֧וֹת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֛ה נָסְע֥וּ הָעָ֖ם חֲצֵר֑וֹת וַיִּהְי֖וּ בַּחֲצֵרֽוֹת׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
From Kivros Hataavoh the people journeyed to Chatzeiros, and they stayed in Chatzeiros.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the people journeyed from Qivrot-hatta᾽ava to Ḥażerot, and at Ḥażerot they made a stay.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
From Kivroth Hata'avah the people traveled to Chatzeiroth, and they abode in Chatzeiroth.



## Chapter 12

###### Numbers 12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:1)


וַתְּדַבֵּ֨ר מִרְיָ֤ם וְאַהֲרֹן֙ בְּמֹשֶׁ֔ה עַל־אֹד֛וֹת הָאִשָּׁ֥ה הַכֻּשִׁ֖ית אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָקָ֑ח כִּֽי־אִשָּׁ֥ה כֻשִׁ֖ית לָקָֽח׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Miriam and Aharon spoke about Moshe concerning the Cushite woman that he married, for, he married a Cushite woman.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Miryam and Aharon spoke against Moshe because of the Kushite woman whom he had taken, for he had taken a Kushite woman.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of [his divorcing] the Cushite woman [(Zipporah, called "Cushite" because she was extremely beautiful in all respects)] that he had taken; for he had taken a Cushite woman, [and now he had divorced her]. [Miriam was with Tzipporah when Moses was told that Eldad and Medad were prophesying in the camp, and she heard her exclaim: "Woe to the wives of these men upon whom prophesy has been conferred, and who will separate from their wives just as my husband (Moses) has separated from me!" Miriam thereupon apprised Aaron of this, (wherefore, being the initiator of the talk against Moses, she is mentioned first)].


###### Numbers 12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:2)


וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ הֲרַ֤ק אַךְ־בְּמֹשֶׁה֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה הֲלֹ֖א גַּם־בָּ֣נוּ דִבֵּ֑ר וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע יְהֹוָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
They said: “Is it only to Moshe that Adonoy has spoken? Did He not also speak with us?” and Adonoy heard.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And they said, Has the Lord indeed spoken only with Moshe? has he not spoken also with us? And the Lord heard it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And they said: Is it only with Moses that the L-rd has spoken? Has He not spoken also with us? [and we have not separated from our spouses!] And the L-rd heard.


###### Numbers 12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:3)


וְהָאִ֥ישׁ מֹשֶׁ֖ה עָנָ֣ו מְאֹ֑ד מִכֹּל֙ הָֽאָדָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The man, Moshe [was] most humble, more so than any other person on the face of the earth.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
(Now the man Moshe was very meek, more so than all the men that were upon the face of the earth.)


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the man Moses was extremely humble [lowly and forbearing], more than any man on the face of the earth.


###### Numbers 12:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:4)


וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה פִּתְאֹ֗ם אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶל־מִרְיָ֔ם צְא֥וּ שְׁלׇשְׁתְּכֶ֖ם אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיֵּצְא֖וּ שְׁלׇשְׁתָּֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said, suddenly, to Moshe, Aharon and Miriam: “Come out, all three of you, to the Tent of Meeting,” and the three of them went out.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord spoke suddenly to Moshe, and to Aharon, and to Miryam, Come out you three to the Tent of Meeting. And they three came out.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said suddenly to Moses, to Aaron, and to Miriam ["suddenly," when they (Aaron and Miriam) were unclean through intercourse, and they cried for water (to purify themselves with) — this, by way of impressing upon them that Moses being constantly ("suddenly") subject to a visitation by the Shechinah, did well in separating himself from his wife] (The L-rd said:) The three of you go out to the tent of meeting [(the three were called by a single utterance, something which (within the framework of nature) the mouth is not capable of uttering nor the ear of hearing)]; and the three of them went out.


###### Numbers 12:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:5)


וַיֵּ֤רֶד יְהֹוָה֙ בְּעַמּ֣וּד עָנָ֔ן וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל וַיִּקְרָא֙ אַהֲרֹ֣ן וּמִרְיָ֔ם וַיֵּצְא֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy descended in a pillar of cloud and He stood at the entrance of the Tent, and He called [to] Aharon and Miriam, and both of them went out.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord came down in the pillar of cloud, and stood in the door of the tent, and called Aharon and Miryam: and they both came out.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd descended in a pillar of cloud, and He stood at the door of the tent, and He called Aaron and Miriam [to separate them from Moses, (all of a man's praise not being mentioned to his face, see Genesis 7:1)], and the two of them came forth.


###### Numbers 12:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:6)


וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֣א דְבָרָ֑י אִם־יִֽהְיֶה֙ נְבִ֣יאֲכֶ֔ם יְהֹוָ֗ה בַּמַּרְאָה֙ אֵלָ֣יו אֶתְוַדָּ֔ע בַּחֲל֖וֹם אֲדַבֶּר־בּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
He said: “Please listen to My words. If there will be a prophet among you, [I,] Adonoy, will make Myself known to him in a vision; in a dream I will speak to him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord make myself known to him in a vision, and speak to him in a dream.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And He said: Hear, I pray you, My words. If there be prophets among you, "the L-rd" [i.e., the immanence of My Name] I invest him with in a vision; in a dream I speak to him.


###### Numbers 12:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:7)


לֹא־כֵ֖ן עַבְדִּ֣י מֹשֶׁ֑ה בְּכׇל־בֵּיתִ֖י נֶאֱמָ֥ן הֽוּא׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
That is not the case with My servant, Moshe; in My entire house he is trusted.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
My servant Moshe is not so, for he is the trusted one in all my house.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Not so My servant Moses. In all My house he is trusted.


###### Numbers 12:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Numbers/r/12:8)


פֶּ֣ה אֶל־פֶּ֞ה אֲדַבֶּר־בּ֗וֹ וּמַרְאֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א בְחִידֹ֔ת וּתְמֻנַ֥ת יְהֹוָ֖ה יַבִּ֑יט וּמַדּ֙וּעַ֙ לֹ֣א יְרֵאתֶ֔ם לְדַבֵּ֖ר בְּעַבְדִּ֥י בְמֹשֶֽׁה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Mouth to mouth I spoke to him [i.e., I told him to separate from his wife (see Deuteronomy 5:27-28)], and [in clear] revelation [of My words], and not in riddles; and the configuration [i.e., the "back" (see Exodus 33:23)] of the L-rd does he behold. Why, then, did you not fear to speak against My servant, [even if he were not Moses], against Moses, [even if he were not My servant]!

###### Numbers 14:2

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
I am Adonoy, your God, Who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am Adonoy your God.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Miżrayim, to be your God: I am the Lord your God.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I am the L-rd, [(trusted to reward)], your G-d, [(trusted to exact payment)], who took you out of the land of Egypt to be a G-d to you [i.e., so that you accept My decrees]; I am the L-rd your G-d [ — perforce! (You do not have the option of saying: "We shall not do the mitzvoth and not receive reward.")]



## Chapter 16

###### Numbers 16:1

וַיִּקַּ֣ח קֹ֔רַח בֶּן־יִצְהָ֥ר בֶּן־קְהָ֖ת בֶּן־לֵוִ֑י וְדָתָ֨ן וַאֲבִירָ֜ם בְּנֵ֧י אֱלִיאָ֛ב וְא֥וֹן בֶּן־פֶּ֖לֶת בְּנֵ֥י רְאוּבֵֽן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Korach took, [Korach], the son of Yitzhar the son of Kehos, the son of Levi, and Dasan and Aviram the sons of Eliav, and On the son of Peles, the sons of Reuvein.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Now Qoraĥ, the son of Yiżhar, the son of Qehat, the son of Levi, and Datan and Aviram, the sons of Eli᾽av, and On, the son of Pelet, of the sons of Re᾽uven, took men:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Korach set himself apart [from the midst of the congregation (to contend against the "awarding" of the priesthood to Aaron)], the son of Yitzhar, the son of Kehath, the son of Levi [("the son of Jacob" being omitted in consideration of Jacob's prayer (Genesis 49:6)], and Dathan and Aviram, the sons of Eliav [(of the tribe of Reuven, neighbors of Korach in the southern encampment — "Woe to the wicked one; woe to his neighbor!")], and On, the son of Peleth, sons [i.e., descendants] of Reuven.

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and they rose up before Moshe, with certain of the children of Yisra᾽el, two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, regularly summoned to the congregation, men of renown:
